fields.features_heading: The Terms a Royalty Deal Turns On
fields.features_subheading: A royalty agreement form records what is licensed and on what terms. Six parts keep the numbers straight.
fields.feature_1:
The rate and its base, asked apart

The form asks for the royalty rate and what it is a share of: list price, net sales, or a fixed amount per unit. A rate means little until the form knows what it multiplies.
fields.feature_2:
Splits that have to add up

List each co-writer or co-author with a share. The form will not submit until the shares add up to the whole work, and only then does it ask each person to sign on their phone.
fields.feature_3:
Advances with an earn-out point

Enter the advance beside the royalty per unit. The app divides one by the other and shows how many copies or units must sell before royalties cover the advance and payments start.
fields.feature_4:
Quarterly reports filed against the deal

Licensees file sales through a report form linked to their agreement. The app applies the rate and any minimum and shows the amount due for that quarter next to the sales figure.
fields.feature_5:
A reminder when a statement runs late

Set how many days a licensee has after each quarter to report. When the deadline passes with no report, the app emails the licensee and alerts the rights holder in the app.
fields.feature_6:
Agreements in a repository you control

On paid plans, export the full code of the form and its database to your GitHub repository. Host it on your own servers and keep extending it beside your contract files.

fields.usecase_heading: Royalty Deals That Get Signed and Paid
fields.tab_content_1:
Three writers, one song, shares that add up

Night Ferry has three writers at Marrow Street Music. June Adeyemi takes half, and Caleb Ortiz and Hollis Ward take a quarter each. The form holds the agreement until the shares account for the whole song, then sends it to all three writers to sign. Their signatures sit on one record under the song title.
fields.tab_content_2:
Each paperback pays $1.28 toward a $2,560 advance

Pondhaven Press pays Delia Haskett $1.28 on each copy of her $16 paperback. Her agreement records a $2,560 advance, and the form divides it by the royalty per copy to set the earn-out point at 2,000 copies. Royalty payments to Delia start with copy 2,001.
fields.tab_content_3:
Ravi earns $1,104, which the minimum lifts to $1,500

Every quarter, Tumblewick Toys reports net sales of Ravi Solberg's fox plush through a form tied to his license. Ravi earns 6 cents on every dollar, and Q3 sales of $18,400 come to $1,104. His license sets a $1,500 quarterly minimum, and that is the amount the report shows as due.
fields.tab_content_4:
Sundew's statement, overdue by one day

Sundew Calendars prints four of Marguerite Lowe's photographs under license and owes a sales statement 30 days after each quarter ends. The Q3 statement was due Oct 30 and never came. On Oct 31 the app emails Sundew a reminder and sends Marguerite a card saying the statement is late.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Royalty Agreement Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps that turn your deal terms into a royalty agreement form that collects signatures and chases late reports.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Decide what the royalty is a share of
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Add the advance and any minimum
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down what is licensed, to whom, and for how long. A song split and a character license need different fields. List the kinds of deals you sign before you write a word of the prompt, and note who signs each one.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the base before the rate. A book deal can pay on list price while a toy license pays on net sales. If the base is net sales, define which returns and discounts come off, and both sides will work from the same number.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Record any advance paid up front and any minimum the licensee owes each period. The form keeps both beside the rate, and every report it takes later works out the amount due with them already applied.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose how often licensees report sales, such as every quarter, and how many days they get after each period closes. Those two numbers decide when each statement is due and when the app sends its first reminder.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the parties and the royalty terms into one prompt, along with the reporting schedule. Emergent builds the agreement form and the report form, with the database behind both. Change a field later by asking for it in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Name each party who signs, including every co-writer on a split. The app sends the agreement to each of them and keeps the signatures together on one record. Have a lawyer read the agreement wording before the first real deal goes out.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sign a test agreement between two of your own email addresses, then file a quarterly report that falls under the minimum. Check that the amount due shows the minimum and that the late-statement email arrives the day after the deadline.

faq_plan.q: What is a royalty agreement form?
faq_plan.a: A royalty agreement form records the terms of a deal in which one party pays another for using its work. A royalty is compensation paid for the use of intellectual property or natural resources. The form puts the work and its royalty terms on one record that both parties sign.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a royalty agreement form?
faq_plan.a: List the parties, the royalty base and rate, any advance or minimum, and how often the licensee reports sales. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, and it builds the agreement form, a report form for each period, and the database that holds every deal.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a royalty agreement form include?
faq_plan.a: Start with the licensor and licensee, then the licensed work and its territory and term. Add the rate and its base, any advance or minimum, the reporting period, and a signature line for each party. Royalties are typically paid monthly, quarterly, or annually. Give the period its own field. Emergent builds those fields from a plain-English description.

faq_plan.q: How does a royalty agreement form differ from a flat-fee license?
faq_plan.a: A flat-fee license needs one payment field, while a royalty agreement form needs a rate and a base, plus a report each period. A flat fee stays the same, the way rent does on a rental agreement form. A royalty is typically computed as a percentage of the sales or profit the licensed asset brings in.

faq_plan.q: How does a royalty agreement form work out what is owed?
faq_plan.a: It multiplies the period's base by the rate, then compares the result with any minimum. A licensee selling 800 units at $0.75 a unit owes $600, but under a $1,000 minimum for the period it owes $1,000. Some royalty agreements include a minimum payment like this one. The form keeps it beside the rate and applies it to every report.

faq_plan.q: Can co-writers sign a royalty agreement form online?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The app sends the split agreement to each co-writer and captures every e-signature on one record for the song. Whether those signatures are enforceable for a given deal is a question for a lawyer, not the form.

faq_plan.q: How should a royalty agreement form describe the licensed property?
faq_plan.a: Name it precisely: the title, any catalog or registration number, and the products or formats the license covers. An equipment rental agreement form lists each item by serial number for the same reason. The license agreement also limits how far the asset can be used. State the territory and the term beside the description.

faq_plan.q: How should a royalty agreement form handle an advance?
faq_plan.a: Give the advance its own field, with the date it is paid. Licensing agreements may include an upfront payment or advance on royalties. The app sets each report's royalties against it until the advance is covered. Emergent keeps each agreement and the sales reported against it in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can a royalty agreement form collect quarterly sales reports?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Build a report form tied to each agreement, where the licensee picks the license and enters sales for the period. Licensors may have the right to audit the licensee's records. Keep each report as its own row with the date and who filed it. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps.

faq_plan.q: Who should approve a royalty agreement form before it goes out?
faq_plan.a: Whoever controls the rights and whoever controls the payments. At a small press, that could be the publisher and the finance lead. Route the draft terms through an approval form first. The rate and the advance are then signed off before the agreement reaches the other party.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Royalty Agreement Form That Does the Math on Every Deal' and hero 'Build a royalty agreement form that works out what each deal owes and saves every agreement to a database you own.' cover the whole job (terms, splits, advances, reports); how-to description is one sentence on what the steps achieve.

intent.evidence: Searchers of 'royalty agreement form' get a definition (FAQ 1), the fields to include (FAQ 3, features 1-3), how the money is worked out (FAQ 5, tabs 2-3) and a seven-step build ('01 Start with the deal itself' to '07 Run a test quarter').

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: 'earn-out point', 'net sales', 'quarterly minimum', 'co-writer shares', 'statement 30 days after each quarter ends'; four segments (music, books, product, art licensing).

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'The form asks for the royalty rate...', 'Night Ferry has three writers at Marrow Street Music.', 'Pick the base before the rate.'

craft.evidence: Sentences carry one idea each, e.g. 'Royalty payments to Delia start with copy 2,001.'; QC P2 serial-comma flags checked by hand: all two-item phrases, no list missing a comma.

voice.evidence: Plain verbs and concrete details ('Pondhaven Press pays Delia Haskett $1.28 on each copy of her $16 paperback'); no hype or AI tells. Bolted-on source sentences in the FAQ kept as a note.

truth.evidence: Every world fact matches its quoted source span (accountingtools royalty article: definition, percentage of sales, periodic payment, minimum, advance, audit, license limits). Math checked: 50+25+25=100%; $1.28/$16=8%, $2,560/$1.28=2,000 copies; 6% x $18,400=$1,104 < $1,500 minimum; image rows 6% x $29,800=$1,788, $31,000=$1,860, $27,500=$1,650; Q3 ends Sep 30 + 30 days = Oct 30, reminder Oct 31; FAQ 5 800 x $0.75=$600 < $1,000. Emergent claims map to claims_used (e-signature-capture with legal validity deferred: 'Whether those signatures are enforceable for a given deal is a question for a lawyer, not the form'; step 6 'Have a lawyer read the agreement wording'). Nothing reads as legal advice.

distinct.evidence: Royalty-specific mechanics (rate base, splits, earn-out, minimum, late statements) do not overlap the operating, shareholder or corporate resolution siblings; no sibling primary in any heading.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic written questions, each answered in its first sentence ('It multiplies the period's base by the rate, then compares the result with any minimum.'); hub link in item 2; links to rental agreement, equipment rental agreement and approval form pages; no brand or file-format questions.
